title: Canonical tower reductions commute with shifts
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $T$. Put $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$ for $n\geq1$. Use the strict semilinear coefficient towers $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], their ordinary derived category $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ with its shift [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the exact evaluations $C\mapsto C_n$ and the canonical derived reduction maps $\rho^C_{n,m}:(C_n)_{R_m}\to C_m$, $m\leq n$, of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and derived scalar extension $(-)_{R_m}:D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^m)$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. For $r\in\mathbf Z$ let $\epsilon_{n,r}(C):(C[r])_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n[r]$ be the shift comparison of the exact evaluation [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and let $\sigma_r(M):(M[r])_{R_m}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{R_m}[r]$ be the shift comparison of the triangulated functor $(-)_{R_m}$. Then for every $C\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, every $r\in\mathbf Z$ and all $m\leq n$,
$$\epsilon_{m,r}(C)\circ\rho^{C[r]}_{n,m}=\rho^C_{n,m}[r]\circ\sigma_r(C_n)\circ(\epsilon_{n,r}(C))_{R_m}.$$
No flatness of $R_m$ over $R_n$, boundedness or constructibility is assumed.

proof.text: For any additive functors F,H,G and natural transformation alpha:F composed with H to G, its termwise cochain transformation commutes with every integer shift. The mapHomologicalComplex shift comparisons have identity components. In degree j both sides are alpha at K^(j+r), and the two differentials have the same shift sign. This calculation applies to the ordinary reduction without using its tensor formula.

proof.text: Apply rightKanExtension_coherentShift to the actual scalar cochain universal pair. Its chosen coherent shift is definitionally spTowerScalarShift, and choose_spec says its universal counit epsilon commutes with shifts. Whisker the evaluation factorization, epsilon and the termwise reduction, insert the standard functor associators, and compose them with the inverse evaluation factorization. All these natural transformations commute with shifts. The representative formula identifies this composite with precomposition of rho by Q.

proof.text: To descend shift compatibility, apply localization natTrans_ext to the two shift-square natural transformations. On QK, the shift-compatible precomposition from the preceding step gives the desired square after precomposing with F(S(Q shift comparison)). Naturality of rho gives that precomposition, and its isomorphism can be cancelled. Thus rho commutes with shifts on all derived objects. Expand the composite functor shift comparison and take the component at C to obtain exactly the displayed equation. No universal comparison is inverted.
